risks.risk: The evidential point may be a familiar application of hermeneutical justice or inclusive deliberation rather than a distinct contribution.
risks.trigger: A full primary-source comparison finds the same limit on treating consensus, silence, or complaint reductions as evidence of deliberative success.
risks.current_limit: Source packet contains excerpts only; Young was available only as an opening search-index excerpt.

risks.risk: The scope rule can be controlled by reformers who define their stated aims and foreseeable costs narrowly.
risks.trigger: Affected participants have no bounded procedure to challenge the reform's declared scope.
risks.current_limit: The proposal says the boundary should be public and revisable but gives no decision procedure.

risks.risk: A usable route may be impossible to measure prospectively or may impose a large burden on a process with limited time.
risks.trigger: Testing uptake requires unlimited translation, repeated review, or costly procedural expansion.
risks.current_limit: The existing criteria name content, recognition, answerability, and burden without a threshold.

risks.risk: Conceptual negotiation may itself constitute the object-level disagreement, so the candidate may misclassify a term dispute as a suppressed policy objection.
risks.trigger: The alleged objection has no independently traceable challenge to the reform's reasons or foreseeable effects.
risks.current_limit: The assigned Plunkett–Sundell excerpts distinguish these levels but do not settle the candidate's case.

risks.risk: Independent outcome evidence may justify a reform while leaving deliberative quality unknown; the proposal could overstate what such evidence establishes.
risks.trigger: The argument slides from policy effectiveness to deliberative success or vice versa.
risks.current_limit: The narrowed claim separates those conclusions, but no empirical case was tested.

not_checked: Empirical performance of any real complaint, translation, or review system.
Full text of metadata-only Fricker 2007 and Plunkett–Sundell 2013 sources.
